item.title: Gambit 1.3.0
item.description:
# Gambit 1.3.0
Released November 21, 2026.
## Your Mac, from your phone
The iPhone can now show you what your Mac is looking at, and talk to the agent running there. It is in Settings › Pairing › Your Mac, and on a button beside Tabs once you have paired.
- **A live view of the tab.** Not a still that refreshes: a frame loop, so a page in motion updates as fast as it can be encoded and a still one costs almost nothing. Pinch to zoom, double-tap to zoom at a point, or open it full screen and read a document properly — a desktop page on a phone needs magnification, not a bigger box.
- **The Mac's agent, on the Mac's pages.** Type into the composer and the turn runs *there*, on the Mac's tabs with the Mac's sign-ins. The transcript streams back with each step as a sentence — "Read 4 results on Google Drive · 1.2s" — and Markdown and tables render as they do in the phone's own agent pane.
- **Read-only mirroring.** Nothing in the phone can click, type or navigate on your Mac. That is by construction, not a setting: no route takes an action.
## Pairing without Tailscale installed
The phone runs its own tailnet node now, so a `.ts.net` code works with nothing installed but Gambit. It needed no VPN entitlement — the Go library Gambit links is a userspace network stack, not a packet tunnel.
## Fixed
- **Signing out of Tailscale stranded the node.** Sign-in pages are minted once in the lifetime of the process, so a node that had been signed out could never sign back in: the card spun on "asking Tailscale for a sign-in page" for ever. It now asks again, and the page arrives in about a second.
- **Sign out, from either app.** There was no way to leave a tailnet before. Both platforms now offer it, behind a confirmation.
- **The address bar showed tracking data.** A Google search rendered in full is 227 characters, most of it protobuf base64 — it looked like a rendering fault, and it was one. The pill now shows `google.com/search?q=your words`.
## The rest
Everything since 1.0 is in `CHANGELOG.md`; 1.1 and 1.2 shipped without their sections being cut, so this release's notes include them.
